  3.  Chamber of Commerce Report

  Danielle Borja, President/CEO for the Greater Conejo Chamber of Commerce
  highlighted recent and upcoming events of the Greater Conejo Chamber of

  was very successful, the Chamber launched the Elevate Conejo Valley program,
  offering Small Business workshops in partnership with the Ventura County
  Economic Development Collaborative. Lastly, she announced that nominations are

  1.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR CONDITIONAL USE  PERMIT  NO.  18-001,
  MODIFICATION NO. 1: RESOLUTION NO. 2286-23

  Mayor Pearl opened the Public Hearing. Senior Planner Sinkula presented a
  request to approve Conditional Use Permit No. 18-001, Modification No. 1 to
  authorize the continued operation of an adult day health care facility located at 5703
  Corsa Avenue, Suite No. 100. Applicants Sania Sameri and Kiana Samar
  Bahadoran, on behalf of S & K Health Services doing business as Infinity Adult Day
  Health Care.

  Ms. Sinkula provided background of the operation and stated that on February 28,
  2018, the City Council approved CUP No. 18-001 to authorize the establishment of

  j  an adult day health care facility operated by Infinity Adult Day Health Care. The
  subject site is in the Mixed Use Corsa Zone of the North Business Park, and the
  operation of an adult day health care facility is allowed but conditionally permitted
  within this Zone. The subject CUP expired on February 28, 2023, and the applicants
  have requested an extension of the permit term. The applicant is not requesting any
  modifications to the permit. Staff recommended a permit term of ten years, such that
  the expiration of the subject CUP would be extended to March 22, 2033.

  On March 1, 2023 the Land Use Committee (Davis/Honig) reviewed the request for
  a time extension and recommended that the request be moved forward to the full
  City Council for hearing.

2.  PUBLIC HEARING FOR PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT NO. 22-001:
  RESOLUTION NO. 2287-23

  Mayor Pearl opened the Public Hearing. Senior Planner Sinkula presented Planned
  Development Permit No. 22-001 authorizing the conversion of an existing movie
  theater into two new restaurant suites and one new retail suite, the installation of a
  new outdoor dining area, and an exterior remodel of the shopping center located at
  4061 Lakeview Canyon Road. David Chau, applicant, filed the request on behalf of
  Marshall Gross.

  Ms. Sinkula provided background of the proposed County Line Shopping Center
  remodel and stated that on May 16, 2022, a PDP application was filed by David
  Chau, on behalf of Marshall Gross, that requests authorization for a change of use
  to convert an existing movie theater into three separate new suites that would
  include two restaurant suites and one retail suite. The project also proposes
  constructing a new outdoor dining area to service the two new restaurant suites and

  Commercial Planned Development (CPD) Zone. A PDP is required for a change in
  use of a structure for which a PDP was never approved. The County Line Shopping

  is now required to authorize the proposed conversion of the movie theater to
  restaurant and retail uses.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  March 22, 2023  5

  PUBLIC HEARINGS (continued):

l  The proposed improvements will be completed in phases, with priority given to the
  conversion of the movie theater into restaurant and retail space and necessary
  repairs to the exterior of the convenience store at the south end of the center. The
  applicants are planning to remodel the exterior of the bank building on the site as
  the final phase of the project, and the recommended conditions of approval include
  a provision authorizing the remodel of this portion of the site using the same exterior
  materials as proposed for the main shopping center building. The applicant also
  plans to replace all signage on the site, and the recommended conditions of approval
  include a provision requiring the applicant to apply for a sign program to authorize
  all new signage and ensure cohesiveness of design and materiality across the
  shopping center.

  Staff recommended approval of the subject PDP request, as the proposed
  conversion of the movie theater to restaurant and retail uses is consistent with the
  permitted uses in the CPD Zone, and the exterior remodel is compatible with the
  architectural styles and earthen tone color palette of surrounding development.

  On November 2, 2022, the subject request was reviewed by the Land Use
  Committee (then Mayor Pro Tern Pearl and Councilmember Honig). The Committee
  noted that the proposed project updated the design and style of the shopping center
  in a manner consistent with the City's design standards. The Committee discussed
  the one-way circulation of the existing parking lot and noted the safety issues caused
  by noncompliance of drivers going the wrong way. The Committee directed the
  applicants to work with the City's Traffic Engineer to revise the parking lot layout to
  address this concern and bring the revised layout back to the Committee for review.
  Councilmember Honig also requested that the applicant fully enclose the proposed
  new outdoor dining area with a low perimeter wall on both sides to provide a barrier
  between patrons of the dining area and vehicles in the parking lot and on Lakeview
  Canyon Road.

  On March 1, 2023 the Land Use Committee (Davis/Honig) reviewed the proposed
  the proposed changes to the parking lot layout and the revision to extend the outdoor
  dining area perimeter wall. The applicant proposes to improve the circulation in the
  parking lot by converting two of the one-way aisles to two-way directional flow. This
  proposed change will not affect the number of parking spaces and will require only
  minor modifications to existing curbs and landscaping. The City's Traffic Engineer
  additionally recommended the removal of an existing light post that adversely
  impacts parking lot circulation on the north end of the site, which is included in the
  recommended conditions of approval. The Committee also discussed the condition
  of the concrete driveway off Agoura Road that accesses the rear of the shopping
  center and requested that the applicant repair the driveway as part of the overall site
  improvements, which is included in the recommended conditions of approval. The
  Committee recommended that the request be moved forward to the full City Council
  for a public hearing.

  1.  Engineering Department Report

  City Engineer Hughes highlighted various items from the Engineering Department
  Status Report. She noted that the Pickleball Courts specifications will be coming
  back with a more robust financial impact section and addressing all additional
  modifications requested by City Council. Related to sidewalk improvements, the
  Measure R Letter of No Prejudice has been executed by the Los Angeles County
  Metropolitan Transportation Authority. Staff wase still working on the easement
  agreements with the homeowner associations, and once resolved, plans and
  specifications will be presented to the City Council for approval. The Sidewalk
  Master Pian next steps wiii be presented it to the Public Safety Advisory Boaid.
  Lastly, the North Santa Monica Bay Watershed Area Steering Committee is going to
  an in person format for their meetings on April 13 with no meeting held in March.

  City of Westlake Village  March 22, 2023  7

  2.  Planning Department Report

  Planning Director Forbes provided the Planning Department Status Report and
  stated that staff continues to work on the Development Impact Fee study with a
  potential new special assessment district for the North Business Park Specific Plan
  area. He anticipated coming to City Council in May 2023. Staff is also working on
  fence and wall regulations and bringing them to the Land Use Committee in April
  2023. Lastly, the new Waste Management cart rollout has been completed to the
  residential neighborhoods.

  3.  Cultural Recreation Report

  Community Services Coordinator Roush reported on three events for Earth Day
  2023 - April 15, 2023 from 9 am - noon: Wishbone Trail Clean-up in partnership
  with Conejo Open Space Conservation Agency; April 22, 2023 from 5-9 pm: Earth
  Day Festival at Community Park which will include vendors, ecofriendly crafts,
  sunset yoga, and a family friendly movie; April 29, 2023 from 9 am - 1 pm: Shred
  Event at City Hall for residents, allowing4 bags or boxes to be shred. Residents can

NEW BUSINESS:

1.  FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 ASSESSMENTS FOR LIGHTING AND LANDSCAPE
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICTS: RESOLUTION NOS. 2288-23 THROUGH 2293-23

  City Engineer Hughes presented the proposed Fiscal Year 2023-24 assessments
  for Lighting Maintenance Assessment District No. 1, Landscape Maintenance
  Assessment District No. 1, and Westlake Spectrum Local Landscape Assessment
  District No. 15. Ms. Hughes stated the City Council must annually review and levy
  assessments against all assessable parcels within the three districts for installation,
  operation and maintenance of certain street landscaping and street lighting
  improvements.

  Ms. Hughes provided background on each assessment district, stating the
  assessment amounts are not proposed for any adjustments at this time. She
  requested the Council adopt Resolution Nos. 2288-23 through 2293-23 and set a
  Public hearing of public protests of the Districts to be held at the April 26, 2023 City
  Council meeting and that staff be directed to give notice of the Public Hearing.

  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved that City Council Adopt Resolution Nos. 2288-
  23 through 2293-23 and set a Public hearing of public protests of the Districts to be
  held at the April 26, 2023 City Council meeting and that staff be directed to give
  notice of the Public Hearing. Councilmember Halpern seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Halpern, Mcsweeney, Honig, Mayor Pro Tern
  Davis, and Mayor Pearl.

2. 2022 GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT

  Planning Director Forbes provided an overview of the 2022 General Plan Annual
  Progress Report as required by State law and noted that the purpose of the report
  was to provide information on the City's progress toward meeting its share of
  regional housing needs and to report on the status of General Plan implementation
  programs.

  Mr. Forbes reviewed the status of each General Plan chapter including Community
  Development (Land Use Element), Infrastructure and Community Service
  (Circulation Element), Natural Resources (Conservation and Open Space
  Elements), Hazards (Safety and Noise Elements), and Housing Element. He noted
  that the website and publications on housing programs were updated to add
  information on housing assistance programs, fair housing, voucher programs and
  rebates. The Zoning Ordinance was updated for consistency with State law related
  to Accessory Dwelling Units, density bonus, emergency shelters and other special
  housing types.

  Staff will submit all required documentation to the State Office of Planning and
  Research and the State Department of Housing and Community Development by
  the April 1, 2023 deadline.

  Councilmember Honig moved that the City Council receive and file the 2022 General
  Plan Annual Progress Report. Councilmember Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  Davis, and Mayor Pearl.
